Combined MPLPB is a closed local ledger with tools for raw-material sorting,
bounded source questions, documentary inspection and retained work history.
Its browser, native CLI and agent adapters preserve the existing authority rules.

**One owner returns; two stop; none refuses.** This is the ownership rule:
one eligible owner may return its page, competing owners stop for ambiguity,
and no eligible owner means refusal. A returned page is not automatically a
supported answer. Strict answering additionally checks eligible source wording
under the finite proof rules. Source integrity does not establish historical truth.

**Research status:** attributable engineering contribution and technical case
study, still being tested. The particular combination may be distinctive;
it is not proven world-first. Independent historical semantic accuracy and
shared-service production readiness remain unestablished.

| Part | What it does | What its output establishes |
|---|---|---|
| [Offline sorter](docs/PREPROCESSING_SORTER.md) | Extracts keys, dates, headers, references and repeated phrases from raw UTF-8 text/Markdown, with exact source spans | Textual observations and optional review edges; no supported answers |
| [Optional sorter review aids](docs/SORTER_REVIEW_OPTIONS.md) | Rank exact/search-neighbor wording and propose source-linked reviews | Inspectable suggestions; no ownership or source support |
| [Candidate review workspace](docs/CANDIDATE_REVIEW_WORKSPACE.md) | Compare processed passages with eligible originals, explore unmatched topics and inspect disagreements | Processed material stays outside approved evidence; original approval never transfers |
| [Ledger and provenance gate](docs/PROVENANCE_GATE.md) | Keeps sealed pages, revisions, ancestry, restrictions and current serving eligibility | Which source bytes and pages may be inspected under the selected policy |
| [Strict answer reader](docs/GENERAL_ANSWER_PIPELINE.md) | Checks eligible body statements against bounded question/proof rules | Source-attributed support where established; ambiguity or refusal otherwise |
| [Page and source inspection](docs/PAGE_RETRIEVAL.md) | Retrieves an eligible owner page or keeps matching sources separate | Inspectable pages/bundles, not a factual answer merely because retrieval succeeded |
| [Documentary research](docs/HISTORICAL_RECONSTRUCTION_ENGINE.md) | Separates checked source assertions, exact wording comparisons, question parts and candidate relations | Checked portions and unresolved evidence; no automatic event identity or historical truth |
| [Conversation and reference library](docs/CHAT_WORKFLOW.md) | Offers local Chat, Serious and off-the-record modes, bounded follow-ups, dictionary lookup and library routing | Conversation, context and source evidence retain distinct labels |
| [Collections and acquisition](docs/EXPLORATION_COLLECTIONS.md) | Imports supplied text and permitted captures into local collections | Captured/supplied sources with provenance; acquisition does not authenticate testimony |
| [Specialist work](docs/SPECIALIST_CONTINUITY_API.md) | Retains tasks, claims, revisions, capabilities, attempts and handoffs | Recoverable work history; a saved claim or completion statement is not proof of execution |
| [Integration](docs/AGENT_MIDDLEWARE.md) | Exposes the existing engine through the page-local JavaScript API and native adapters | The same decisions and restrictions; client success is not answer support |

Python 3.8+ is the declared native minimum; CI exercises Python 3.12. The core
runtime uses the standard library and needs no model or inference account.
Network acquisition, hosted crawling and optional models have separate requirements.
The root `index.html` is the desktop entry point. GitHub Pages serves the generated
`dist/index.html` through its deployment workflow, not the unbuilt root file.
[Package contents and installation](docs/INSTALLATION.md).
From a source checkout, this example uses explicitly fictional development files:

```bash
python -m mplpb_work.sorter sort tests/fixtures/sorter \
  --mode not-compared --output /tmp/mplpb-observations-new.json
python -m mplpb_work.sorter sort tests/fixtures/sorter \
  --mode compare --output /tmp/mplpb-comparison-new.json
python -m mplpb_work.sorter peruse /tmp/mplpb-comparison-new.json \
  --sources tests/fixtures/sorter
python -m mplpb_work.sorter export-retired /tmp/mplpb-comparison-new.json \
  --sources tests/fixtures/sorter --ledger /tmp/mplpb-snapshot-new
python -m mplpb_answers validate /tmp/mplpb-snapshot-new --strict
```

Use your own raw-material directory instead of the fixture directory. Outputs must
be new and outside the input tree; use fresh names for repeat runs. `/tmp` is a
POSIX example path; use an appropriate temporary directory on Windows.

Both modes emit **identical nodes, spans, source hashes and provisional statuses**.
Not-compared stops at observations. Compare adds non-authoritative review edges;
matching subjects never force event identity, and missing intermediate records
stop links. The native snapshot is sealed and retired before publication. Existing
`validate` and `show` accept it for inspection; `gate` and `ask` withhold it under
all three profiles. It must not be reactivated as factual evidence.

Sorting does not automatically admit originals for supported answering. Use the
existing source-management/import workflow with the originals' actual permissions,
provenance and delivery policy. [Input/output contract and commands](docs/PREPROCESSING_SORTER.md).

The Synonym Ranker keeps exact and neighbor signals distinct. The Candidate Relater
retains unresolved references, possible corrections and wording reviews. The review
workspace compares processed text with eligible originals, shows both evidence
statuses, and keeps exploration separate from strict proof admission.

Replace `PROCESSED_DIRECTORY` and `NATIVE_LEDGER` with your own source directories;
use fresh output names outside both input collections:

```bash
python -m mplpb_work.sorter_suggestions sort PROCESSED_DIRECTORY --mode compare \
  --query 'Who received the report?' --synonym-ranker --candidate-relater \
  --output NEW_SUGGESTIONS.json
python -m mplpb_work.sorter sort PROCESSED_DIRECTORY --mode compare --output NEW_GRAPH.json
python -m mplpb_work.candidate_workspace build NEW_GRAPH.json \
  --processed PROCESSED_DIRECTORY --originals NATIVE_LEDGER \
  --question 'Who received the report?' --output NEW_WORKSPACE.json
python -m mplpb_work.candidate_workspace peruse NEW_GRAPH.json \
  --processed PROCESSED_DIRECTORY --originals NATIVE_LEDGER --workspace NEW_WORKSPACE.json
```

The workspace takes the base sorter graph. Every processed passage/conclusion is
**candidate for review** and **Exploratory · outside MPLPB-approved evidence.**
Eligible-original citations show their own status. Matching an original never
approves a processed copy. One eligible owner returns its page and independently
checked strict evidence; competing owners require disambiguation; no owner retains
labeled exploration without returning support through that ownership route.

Review has its own bounded passage/character budget, with explicit truncation;
it never consumes strict proof slots. Perusal rechecks source bytes, permissions,
eligibility and decisions. These are native/CLI tools, including the installed
wheel; this update adds no browser workspace. The standalone multi-source strict
pipeline remains distinct from the workspace's single-page ownership panel.
[Full workspace commands and boundaries](docs/CANDIDATE_REVIEW_WORKSPACE.md).

Every processed passage and proposed conclusion has status **candidate for review**, with **Exploratory · outside MPLPB-approved evidence.** Eligible-original endpoints carry their own citation and profile status. An exact copy, synonym, reference or correction candidate never transfers approval to processed material.

```sh
python -m mplpb_work.sorter sort PROCESSED --mode compare --output SORTER.json
python -m mplpb_work.candidate_workspace build SORTER.json --processed PROCESSED --originals LEDGER --question 'Who wrote the Redwood memorandum?' --output REVIEW.json
python -m mplpb_work.candidate_workspace peruse SORTER.json --processed PROCESSED --originals LEDGER --workspace REVIEW.json
```

Use `--topic 'lunar lichens'` for exploration without a question, or alongside a question to explore a different topic. Use `--profile internal`, `lab` or `external`; optional `--as-of` reuses the native serving view. The ledger must be a directly resolved collection of native originals. The workspace does not import, revise, retire or approve any source, follow external links or invoke a model. Outputs must be new files outside processed sources and the original ledger.
## Two visible statuses and two budgets

The ownership panel uses the existing ownership algorithm after intersecting its pages with the reader's current evidence gate. Gate exclusions, hashes, lineage, permissions, depth, not-for declarations, supersession and field scope govern eligibility. A small private optional path filter in the native ownership reader avoids duplicating that algorithm; default callers behave identically. Sorter candidates and synonyms never enter the owner set.

| Eligible owners | Workspace behavior |
|---|---|
| One | Return its page with eligible-source status. Call the existing strict pipeline on originals, without any processed hints; body evidence must independently establish support. |
| Two or more | Keep eligible competitors visible and ask for disambiguation; withhold the workspace strict answer. |
| None | Report that no supported answer is returned by this ownership route; retain labeled processed-document exploration. |

The single-page owner route and multi-source evidence proof are distinct existing capabilities. H05's native comparison is complete through the multi-source strict pipeline even though the legacy page-ownership router finds no owner. The optional workspace applies the requested owner-disambiguation policy; it does not replace or relabel the standalone historical reader experiment. Its H05 regression checks the full standalone answer before and after workspace exploration at12 passages/8000 characters. Workspace ownership refusal is not a lost witness or a strict-budget failure.

`--strict-passages` and `--strict-chars` configure the unchanged strict call. `--exploration-passages` (default24) and `--exploration-chars` (default16000) charge distinct processed and original review spans separately from strict proof. The same span is charged once within its own source domain; a processed copy and its eligible original are distinct. No exploration hint consumes a strict slot. Both budgets report truncation, and the ownership panel can withhold a strict answer while processed exploration remains available.

Exploration uses the existing native retrieval on eligible originals, with an explicitly bounded discovery pool (at most64 passages/64000 characters). `--scan-passages` bounds processed hits and the original pool; `--pair-checks` bounds comparisons. Output is capped at32MiB. Four-word comparison uses at most256 lexical tokens per statement, including unique processed/original phrases; it does not require repetition within processed files. Search truncation, display truncation and core sorter extraction limits are explicit. Unshown material remains in the separately pinned sorter graph; missing matches do not establish historical absence.

Exact wording, literal record references, possible corrections, opposing polarity recognized by the existing small action grammar, and literal four-word phrase review are distinct. Quoted or qualified references retain a separate unresolved-scope label. References name documents; a shown target context does not resolve the intended earlier claim or the correction's field/time. Synonyms and shared topic words rank processed search hits only; they never generate a source link. Four-word phrase matches are lexical review cues, not relationships. Identity, chronology, causation, correction applicability and historical truth remain unresolved.

Processed statements retain sorter occurrence/node IDs, raw source hashes, exact UTF-8 byte spans and review annotations. Original endpoints retain the eligible native revision, canonical body coordinates and a reversible raw UTF-8 excerpt. The existing round-trip projection maps HTML entities/layout without pretending canonical characters are raw bytes. Native-page byte coordinates are explicitly distinguished from external acquisition coordinates. Processed-only topics, unmatched statements, unresolved references and processed disagreements remain explorable under their non-authoritative labels.

Perusal reloads sources and replays the whole workspace, including eligibility, ownership and strict decision. Changed/corrupt sources, revoked permissions, altered decisions, even resealed authority promotion refuse replay. This establishes source/decision fidelity, not semantic correctness of a proposed relationship.

[Workspace controls](../tests/test_candidate_workspace.py) cover all three owner outcomes, missing body support, processed contradictions, processed-only topics, quoted/conditional corrections, unresolved targets, Unicode/entity byte mapping, permission/integrity changes, forged promotion, separate budgets, CLI replay and H05 preservation. The initial workspace completed22 native replays unchanged and five public-source demonstrations, and passed1265 extracted-ZIP tests. A later disconnected-word control reproduced an unwanted broad lexical suggestion; its outputs and failure are retained. The conservative version uses existing four-word phrase observations. That trial passed1266 tests but a new positive phrase control and installed-wheel check exposed separate omissions, retained in its [report](../evaluation/candidate-review-workspace/2026-11-18-conservative/REPORT.md). The runtime repair passes both the positive and disconnected-word controls and an isolated installed-wheel smoke; its new frozen full execution is pending. The earlier [four-arm study](../evaluation/sorter-first-originals/2026-11-18-witness-admission-final/REPORT.md) remains frozen at2/22 complete answers. Independent human and unseen-original evaluation remain NOT RUN.

The [final runtime report](../evaluation/candidate-review-workspace/2026-11-18-runtime/REPORT.md) completes22 native replays unchanged, five source-linked workspace executions/fresh replays,1267 extracted-ZIP regressions and an isolated installed-wheel check. All15 exact candidates remain;49 literal phrase cues replace164 broad word-overlap suggestions, with39 processed passages shown versus28 in v1. These are unverified textual navigation cues; independent semantic accuracy remains unassessed. Pair/display bounds do not cap the existing native gate/index setup; actual read and processing costs are retained.

**One owner returns; two stop; none refuses.** Eligible ownership controls page
selection. It does not waive provenance or body-support checks. A returned page,
a candidate graph, a source bundle, model-assisted interpretation and a strict
supported answer retain distinct labels. No document seal proves historical truth.

| Part | Available behavior | Remaining boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Raw-text sorter | Exact UTF-8 source spans, keys/dates/references, identical nodes across modes, optional review edges | Lexical extraction is incomplete; comparisons do not resolve historical identity |
| Native sorter snapshot | Sealed, strictly validated, exact graph roundtrip; inspected by the unchanged reader | Retired and withheld under every profile; never a source of accepted historical facts |
| Ledger/gates | Revisions, ancestry, source hashes, delivery profiles, exclusions and current eligibility | Integrity/authorship/truth remain separate |
| Strict answering | Finite source-body proofs, explicit diagnostics, conflicts, checked partials and refusals | Many ordinary historical constructions remain unsupported |
| Documentary inspection | Source units/layer hints, literal comparisons, obligations, bounded relations and original-byte mapping where available | Missing links, OCR/quotation problems and ambiguous identities stop completion |
| Application | Native/browser collections, deterministic conversation, references, local context and procedures | Saved user context is not ledger evidence; arbitrary conversation/prose understanding is not established |
| Work and integration | Scoped specialist continuity, host receipts, JavaScript transport and native local MCP | A successful tool/receipt is not historical truth, task execution proof or shared-service readiness |
| Optional acquisition/models | Explicit source capture/crawler setup and separate local/browser helper paths | Deployment, device behavior and semantic efficacy need their own evidence |

The reconstruction path extends the existing strict documentary checker and reversible prose investigation. It does not replace either engine. Source integrity, quotation fidelity, typed statement support, candidate interpretation, human review and historical truth remain separate states.

```sh
python -m mplpb_answers reconstruct LEDGER "Compare the wording in the two accounts."
python -m mplpb_answers reconstruct LEDGER "Why was the expedition delayed, and what resource supported its return?"
python -m mplpb_answers reconstruct LEDGER "When was the report published?" --profile external
python -m tools.reconstruct_original map --ledger LEDGER --question QUESTION --output NEW_REPORT
```

The JSON report includes the existing native answer, individually checked claims and unresolved obligations, reversible candidate propositions/graph, documentary units and layer hints. Existing Ask/API/browser routes retain the answer-contract-v1 behavior. New relationship rules remain partial unless the established complete-answer conditions are satisfied; a literal difference or causal assertion alone never resolves the whole historical question.

`PassageIndex.documentary_units` exposes canonical offsets, complete-boundary flags, source IDs/hashes and inferred documentary layers. Transcript, editorial, quotation, annotation, correspondence and site-chrome hints are derived inspection structure, not new source authority. Uppercase source labels can delimit units without supplying answer facts. Wrapped lines remain unchanged. Long/OCR fragments and exhausted limits remain visible. Original-byte mapping is resolved lazily with `tools.source_roundtrip.original_passage(CORPUS, IMPORT_RECEIPT, UNIT_OR_CITATION)`; null mapping fields do not mean original bytes were independently checked.

The existing kernel re-reads eligible sources and parses complete native units. New finite rules cover explicit because-of passive assertions, resource-provision statements, before/after statements with separate publication/revision/receipt roles, and explicit passive by-phrases. Arguments, negations and time expressions remain literal. They do not authenticate actors, normalize an uncertain date, establish actual execution, or independently prove a source's causal assertion true. Unsupported quotations, conditions and ambiguous prior context stop acceptance. In particular, damaged OCR quotation state can still block otherwise useful Apollo summary statements.

Exact comparisons use complete native paragraph units, including semicolon-separated originals. The checker computes token alignment independently from current source bytes. All equal/insert/delete/replace segments are retained in the structured proposition; the display previews the first twelve alignment segments. The comparison establishes differences between those two units only, not version order, source authenticity, historical correction, motive, responsible editor or absence elsewhere in an incompletely examined document.

The graph is a view of existing reversible proposition/connection mappings. Documentary appearances, actor mentions and event candidates have distinct nodes. Every edge retains source anchors, state dependencies and unresolved identity/link issues. Similar names, subjects, dates or text never merge event candidates. Candidate graph edges never receive strict support automatically. Date candidates preserve their existing roles and do not become a historical timeline by sorting.

For optional local model interpretation, pass `--reader-model INSTALLED_MODEL` and optionally `--reader-endpoint http://127.0.0.1:11434`. This reuses the existing bounded local-reader plan/read/review schema, model digest checks, exact-citation validation and loopback-only transport. Model-generated claims remain assisted output, never historical truth or independent evaluation. No weights are downloaded and no cloud service is required. Live-model efficacy remains unmeasured without an installed model.

Bounds include the caller's passage/character limits; four obligations and twelve proposals; 200,000 scan characters, 1,000 units and 64 action assertions; at most sixty local comparison candidates, two proposed comparisons (four for source-framed requests) and 600 tokens per alignment side; and 160 candidate graph nodes/edges. Full-context omissions and incomplete scans cannot establish historical absence or a complete answer. The source-unit API permits explicitly bounded larger scans; oversized sources bypass immutable caches. Canonical projections and structural parsing cache content only, at most four inputs of at most two million characters each. Current permissions, restrictions, revisions and source hashes are always re-read.

See [review and synthetic-truth rules](HISTORICAL_TRUTH_RULES.md), [crawler admission](../crawler/README.md), and [the versioned experiment](../evaluation/reconstruction-engine/2026-11-17/BASELINE.md). Independent review and unseen evaluation are NOT RUN. A 9/10 rating and the proposed 80%/95%/75%/95% targets require evidence that is not yet available.

Kernel v3 adds a separate completion proof for bounded opening-topic comparisons between a source-declared rough reconstruction and a transcription. It re-reads positive framing statements in canonical body prose, resolves a unique printed work reference and author reference within those declarations, selects the first relevant complete topic paragraph after each declaration, and independently computes both changed and shared wording. All four citations are required: two compared units and two role declarations. Source titles, filenames, ranking and model labels cannot substitute for these witnesses. An ambiguous/missing/qualified role, different work or author, additional factual obligation, incomplete display budget or changed source prevents completion.

The question parser accepts varied literal-comparison wording, not arbitrary historical reasoning. It explicitly rejects unsupported additional obligations rather than silently dropping question words or dates. Completion is scoped to the supplied source-declared appearances. It does not establish manuscript authenticity, that a transcription is the last-ever historical version, a real person's identity, revision motive or historical truth. Other question classes retain their existing support gates. A heading containing Draft may accompany a body-declared rough reconstruction for this text-comparison proof; it remains excluded from unconditional action/execution proofs. Plan, hypothetical and quotation scopes still block role declarations.

For plaintext transcriptions, physical blank paragraphs are used only when their canonical concatenation exactly reproduces the existing projection. Wrapped lines and offsets remain unchanged. Existing admission-manifest paragraphs are excluded from documentary wording/identity evidence. Complete arithmetic comparison does not depend on an exhaustive search for unrelated historical actions, and does not claim whole-document or historical absence. Every necessary selected-source/reference connection is checked separately.

The existing WorkStore can persist claims, evidence, challenges and review decisions with immutable prior revisions. Suggested graph links remain separate from checked source statements and human-reviewed interpretations. New or restricted sources must trigger dependency rechecks. The current derived graph is query-scoped; automatic corpus-wide graph maintenance as pages are imported is still an integration gap. Nothing in this implementation automatically turns a suggested or human-accepted relationship into historical truth.

owner means refusal. All eligibility rules still apply. Strict answering requires
additional support from source body wording. A selected page, a citation, a model

The sorter accepts directories of UTF-8 text and Markdown. It leaves originals
unchanged and records source IDs/hashes, statement text, byte and character spans,
keys, dates, headers, references, action-word candidates and repeated phrase keys.
It works without a model, network connection or manually inserted answer fields.
Its recognizers are finite and incomplete.

| Mode | Nodes and provisional statuses | Edges |
|---|---|---|
| not-compared | Same source-anchored observations in both modes | Containment and textual co-occurrence only |
| compare | Identical nodes, spans, hashes and provisional statuses | Same observation prefix plus review proposals, candidate clusters and possible correction windows |

Compare never merges occurrences into a historical event. Shared subject wording
alone cannot establish identity. Changed bodies under shared identifiers are flagged.
Missing or ambiguous intermediate records stop documentary hops. Correction windows
remain literal, unapplied proposals. Every assessment remains non-authoritative.
The envelope also records mode, digest and any comparison-budget limitations.

```bash

  --mode compare --output NEW_GRAPH.json
python -m mplpb_work.sorter verify NEW_GRAPH.json --sources RAW_DIRECTORY
python -m mplpb_work.sorter peruse NEW_GRAPH.json --sources RAW_DIRECTORY
python -m mplpb_work.sorter export-retired NEW_GRAPH.json \
  --sources RAW_DIRECTORY --ledger NEW_SNAPSHOT_DIRECTORY
```

Output paths must be new and outside the raw input tree. `verify` reloads and
replays source fidelity; it does not verify semantic correctness. Budgets and
exclusions are explicit. Oversized statements or missing records do not justify
inventing a completed relation.

The snapshot is a native sealed page containing the candidate graph. Export
validates the staging ledger, checks exact graph recovery and retires the page

source of historical facts. Do not activate the graph as an answer page.

with the originals' actual ownership, provenance and restrictions. Supplied text
and a URL label are not proof that a site was downloaded or that authorship was
authenticated. Preserve original captures and their versions. PDF extraction/OCR
is outside the sorter. [Complete sorter contract](PREPROCESSING_SORTER.md).

A ledger is a folder of native pages plus its retained history. Pages declare
identity, scope, status, hash, origin/depth and optional ancestry/delivery fields.
The existing writer seals these fields/content; revisions write successors,
withdrawal retains predecessors, and derivatives pin their bases.

The gate checks current source integrity, lineage and serving policy. Retired,
corrupt, stale, restricted or otherwise ineligible pages cannot supply accepted
answer evidence. Current eligibility is rechecked rather than permanently cached.
A title or filename can help locate a source but cannot supply a body assertion.
A pointer is navigation, not evidence or permission to fetch another collection.

Profiles are policy views, not evidence-strength ratings. Lab, internal and external
have different depth/prose settings; explicit restrictions and exclusions remain
binding. Changing a profile is a host/operator decision, not a model permission.
A page becoming visible does not make its content true.

## Run both modes on identical inputs
From the repository root, use a new output directory outside the source directory:

```bash
mkdir /tmp/sorter-example
python -m mplpb_work.sorter sort tests/fixtures/sorter --mode not-compared --output /tmp/sorter-example/raw.json
python -m mplpb_work.sorter sort tests/fixtures/sorter --mode compare --output /tmp/sorter-example/compare.json
python -m mplpb_work.sorter verify /tmp/sorter-example/compare.json --sources tests/fixtures/sorter
python -m mplpb_work.sorter peruse /tmp/sorter-example/compare.json --sources tests/fixtures/sorter --max-items 8
python -m unittest tests.test_sorter -q
```

`not-compared` (also spelled `not compared`) emits observations only: source
occurrences, statements, identifiers, date expressions, headers, reference mentions,
correction cues, action-word candidates and repeated four-word phrase keys. Its
edges are containment and textual co-occurrence; they assert no event identity or
chronology. Literal dates have documentary roles only when a recognized header
supplies that role. Body dates remain unresolved.

`compare` emits **exactly the same sources, nodes, source spans and provisional
statuses**. It appends review edges: candidate identity clusters for shared explicit
identifiers, shared-header/phrase reviews, explicit-reference candidates, possible
corrections and unresolved-reference reviews. Raw edges remain an identical prefix.
Clusters are hyperedge annotations (`members`), never additional nodes. Different
bodies sharing an identifier are flagged, never merged. A shared subject alone
cannot create an identity cluster. Correction windows retain literal expressions,
claim quotation and `applied: false`; no prior claim is rewritten or retired.

Only edges change as documentary data. The envelope also records the chosen mode,
comparison flag, digest and any comparison-budget exhaustion. Comparison cannot
change extraction statuses. Missing or ambiguous targets stop a documentary hop;
unresolved-reference review edges point back to the occurrence being inspected,
not to an invented intermediate record. No transitive chains or inferred chronology
are emitted. Confidence is null; evidence notes explain the lexical proposal basis.

Inputs are recursively discovered `.txt`, `.text`, `.md`, `.markdown` files, strictly
UTF-8. Newlines, BOM and Unicode remain unchanged. Supply extracted document text;
PDF/HTML conversion, OCR and fetching URLs are outside this tool. Hidden entries,
symlinks and nonregular files are excluded. Markdown quotation/fence and conditional
scope recognition is conservative and incomplete, not semantic verification.

* `sources`: relative paths, exact raw SHA-256 hashes and byte lengths.
* `nodes`: stable content/path-derived IDs, `kind`, `span`, `assessment`, and typed
  lexical attributes. Spans include source ID/hash/path, half-open Unicode character
  offsets and half-open original UTF-8 byte offsets. Statement/feature spans carry
  exact `text`; full source-occurrence spans use the original file instead of
  duplicating its text. Paragraph boundaries and explicit identifier-header splits
  are layout candidates, not proof of complete historical documents or events.
* `edges`: `from`, `to`, `kind`, `evidence_nodes`, assessment and proposal notes.
  Compare-only edges have `comparison_only: true`. Identity-cluster edges also carry
  all occurrence `members`, shared identifier namespace/key and changed-body flag.
* `limits`, `complete`, `limits_or_exclusions`, `source_bytes_read`: explicit bounded
  processing diagnostics. Complete means extraction finished within its rules and
  budget, not that all relevant historical evidence exists or was understood.
* `implementation_sha256`, `graph_sha256`: implementation and canonical JSON pins.
  Replay rejects changed source bytes, source inventory, forged proposals and
  implementation drift. Replay establishes extraction fidelity, not semantic truth.
* `prior_assessment`: optional `--prior OLD.json` snapshot retained literally as
  untrusted historical JSON with its own raw hash. Prior assessments are preserved,
  never reused as current matching evidence or authority.

Every assessment has `answer_supported: false`, `source_support_established: false`,
`historical_truth_independently_verified: false`, and serving eligibility unevaluated.
A literal Status header yields a **provisional** current/retired candidate label only;
it cannot change ledger serving state. Event candidates are lexical action-word
observations with no established occurrence or identity.

Default limits: 64 files, 1 MiB/file, 8 MiB total source bytes per pass, 4096 tree
entries, depth12, 4096 nodes, 8192 edges, 2000 statements, 8000 characters/statement,
20000 comparisons, 4096 phrase keys, 32 phrase groups, 1 MiB prior snapshot and
32 MiB serialized output. `--limits limits.json` may only lower these positive
integer limits. Oversized paragraphs are skipped rather than truncated into false
complete statements. Exclusions/caps mark partial output; integrity changes refuse.
Two source passes are counted in `source_bytes_read`; code/metadata reads are not.
There is no OS-enforced wall timeout. Use a trusted local filesystem; path and regular
file checks do not constitute isolation against a hostile OS. Outputs are new files
with mode0600 and never overwrite inputs or existing outputs. Exit2 means refusal.
## Peruse or seal a withheld snapshot using the existing reader

JSON is a research artifact, not a native supported-answer page. `peruse` verifies
fresh source bytes then shows candidates. To store it as a native sealed page:

```bash
python -m mplpb_work.sorter export-retired /tmp/sorter-example/compare.json --sources tests/fixtures/sorter --ledger /tmp/sorter-example/ledger
python -m mplpb_answers validate /tmp/sorter-example/ledger --strict
python -m mplpb_answers show /tmp/sorter-example/ledger SORTER-CANDIDATES
python -m mplpb_answers gate /tmp/sorter-example/ledger 'sorter candidate inspection' --profile lab --json
python -m mplpb_answers gate /tmp/sorter-example/ledger 'sorter candidate inspection' --profile internal --json
python -m mplpb_answers gate /tmp/sorter-example/ledger 'sorter candidate inspection' --profile external --json
python -m mplpb_answers ask /tmp/sorter-example/ledger 'What is Owner for record MAIL-001?' --profile lab --json
python -m mplpb_answers ask /tmp/sorter-example/ledger 'What is Owner for record MAIL-001?' --profile internal --json
python -m mplpb_answers ask /tmp/sorter-example/ledger 'What is Owner for record MAIL-001?' --profile external --json
```

`validate --strict` exits0 with zero errors/warnings: the snapshot is a valid
native page. `show` exits0 and displays it for inspection, even though it is
retired. Each `gate` command exits3 with no eligible sources. Storage acceptance
and inspectability do not confer answer eligibility. Native `show` uses the reader’s
existing normalized text display; use the graph JSON, stored HTML payload and
original source spans for exact whitespace/byte inspection.

Before publishing the new directory, export now runs the existing native validator
against its private staging ledger and independently re-reads the sealed page.
Any native error **or warning**, retirement failure, or changed embedded graph
refuses export and leaves the destination unpublished. The native writer adds its
normal heading; the graph inside the escaped `pre` block must round-trip exactly,
including quoted Unicode, HTML delimiters and original CRLF source strings.
The export receipt includes `native_validation` with errors0, warnings0 and
`graph_roundtrip_verified: true`. These are storage/fidelity checks, not support
or truth judgments. A literal original Status header still cannot activate a page.

The last three commands refuse (exit3), with `answer_supported: false` and empty
`answer_contract.claims`. The native `SORTER-CANDIDATES` page is intact, machine-origin, unratified,
external=no and **retired before publication** from private staging. No existing
ledger is overwritten. The unchanged gate withholds retired evidence in lab/internal;
external also enforces external=no before its retirement check. Tests directly
inspect gate exclusions as well as answers, including historical as-of views. A
failed retirement never publishes a current snapshot at the destination.

Do not reactivate the snapshot as factual evidence. Import unchanged originals
through normal source-management workflows with their real restrictions, ownership
and provenance. The sorter does not know or authorize those policies. Exported
hashes authenticate the snapshot bytes, not the proposed relationships. Graphs may
contain sensitive original excerpts; keep their private output permissions and
apply the source's actual access restrictions.

Fixtures in `tests/fixtures/sorter` are fictional development material. They test
repeated appearances, changed bodies, partial corrections and stopped links; they
are not an independent historical accuracy evaluation. The retained 22-question
historical completion measurements are unchanged by this preprocessing tool.

For a retained graph pair, direct gate exclusions and all three CLI refusal logs,
run `python -m tools.evaluate_sorter --output /tmp/sorter-evidence-new` from the
frozen checkout. This uses fictional fixtures and reports software checks, not
semantic accuracy. Its source/reader code is identical to the frozen implementation.

The existing reader accepts native pages; it does not need to understand the sorter
JSON schema to withhold a retired page. To reproduce compatibility against the
unchanged revision before the sorter existed, prepare a separate checkout:

```bash
git archive --format=zip --output=/tmp/mplpb-reader-base.zip 3df2c6e22f0ef454f3ee67b88d43402a42f63443
python -m zipfile -e /tmp/mplpb-reader-base.zip /tmp/mplpb-reader-base
python -m tools.evaluate_sorter --output /tmp/sorter-plain-reader-new --reader-checkout /tmp/mplpb-reader-base
```

The runner checks that all Python files in `mplpb_answers` and `mplpb_combined`
are byte-identical between the two checkouts. It sorts and exports using the new
code, then invokes native `validate`, `show`, `gate` and `ask` from the specified
plain checkout, with its working directory recorded in each command receipt.
Neither checkout is modified. This distinguishes storage compatibility from
answer eligibility without adapting the reader's grammar or policy checks.

[A Dual-Mode Sorter for MPLPB](research/dual-mode-sorter/README.md), by Mitchell D. McPhetridge, is available in Markdown, plain text and PDF. It documents the implemented stages, dual-mode contract, native publication checks, measured development costs, failed attempts and remaining limitations. Its frozen software results are not independent historical validation. Shared-subject pair proposals consider at most the first16 occurrences per subject; graph completeness does not mean every possible review pair was enumerated.

Header recognition is an observation, not a declaration of the containing file's
identity. Extraction now classifies layout **before occurrence partitioning**.
Recognized fences (backticks or tildes), Markdown blockquotes, explicitly delimited
quotations, forwarded-message frames and bounded example/quotation cues retain
headers as embedded observations. Nested explicit forward frames remain scoped
until their closing markers; an unclosed frame remains review-scoped. A code-fence
closer must use the same marker family, sufficient length and no trailing text.

Header nodes retain `header_context`, `header_role` and
`primary_identity_eligible`. A top-level declaration candidate has
`header_role: record_declaration_candidate`. An embedded appearance has
`header_role: embedded_text_observation` and cannot be a primary identity key.
These fields are derived layout assessments, not proof that a communication is
genuine. An ordinary top-level header stays eligible even if its paragraph also
contains quoted body prose; paragraph scope warnings alone do not decide its role.

Only primary declaration candidates can delimit record occurrences, enter primary
identity-cluster membership, resolve a documentary reference target, or supply the
outer occurrence's declared-status/date-role candidates. The source occurrence
also records `identity_role`: `declared_record_candidate` or
`textual_appearance_only`. The latter means no primary identifier was recognized,
not that the file or a quoted historical communication ceased to exist.

Both modes preserve the same observations and classifications. Compare may append
`embedded_identifier_review` edges with lexical `matching_primary_occurrences`.
These annotations preserve discovery of copied/forwarded material without merging
it into primary cluster membership. An embedded-only target remains unresolved
with `embedded_only_target`; missing and ambiguous targets retain their existing
refusal/review behavior. Shared subjects and similar wording still cannot establish
historical identity or event independence.

These are finite layout rules. Unmarked quotations, ambiguous forwarded archives,
misleading labels and damaged/OCR delimiters can require manual scope review.
No universal document-boundary or historical-identity resolution is claimed. Earlier
graphs remain preserved; the changed implementation fingerprint requires a fresh
replay rather than accepting an old classification silently.

[Scope regression evidence and resume checkpoint](../evaluation/preprocessing-sorter/2026-11-17-header-scope/REPORT.md)
records the supplied probe, the failing pre-fix tests, before/after cluster members,
source-byte checks and verification commands. The checkpoint allows a fresh process
or future worker to recover the task and rules without relying on this session;
it does not measure a minimum AI context size or prove general historical accuracy.

These extensions retain `answer-contract-v1`, the existing eligibility and lineage
checks, relation families, and work-event chain. An intact unique record, its
pinned ancestry, explicit origin/depth, delivery profile, not-for exclusions and
current serving view remain prerequisites. Source integrity does not certify
source truth. Assisted output and relation exploration keep
`answer_supported:false`. The existing deterministic strict-first proof path
remains available before an assisted fallback and labels its output mode `strict`.

```python
from mplpb_answers.pipeline import answer_query
result = answer_query(root, 'What is Owner for record CASE-1?')
result = answer_query(root, 'Inspect owner', record_id='SRC-1@sha256:...', field='Owner')
result = answer_query(root, 'Inspect owner', field='Owner',
    exact_value={'field':'Accession', 'value':'UNIQUE-7788'})
```

The bounded question form is `What is <field> for/of record/event/occurrence
<identifier>?`. Keyword selectors use the same pipeline. Exact record IDs and
pins, explicit body identity keys, and unique field/value selectors route only
after eligibility. Matching eligible pages skip ranking and diversity discounts.
A unique value also retains other appearances sharing its explicit identity key,
so selecting an accession cannot hide a competing owner statement.

Field evidence consists of complete `Label: value` lines in the initial source
body header block. A non-field line, Body, Example or Sample ends that block.
Labels normalize case, underscores and hyphens; values retain their exact source
text. Ledger metadata can route a request but cannot supply a body-field answer.
Repeated conflicting field lines, including later mentions outside the initial
header block, remain separate citations. Later mentions cannot grant field support;
conflicting values produce a conflict and other later context requires review. All competing eligible field passages are checked before any budget
selection. Conflicts never choose a winner. If the display budget cannot retain
all conflicting field passages, the conflict remains unsupported and records an
explicit omitted count.

| Diagnostic | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `exact_field_missing` | An exact route cannot establish the requested explicit body field. |
| `contradictory_passages_pruned` | The budget would omit known competing field passages; the selected subset cannot support an answer. Increase the budget to inspect them all. |
| `event_identity_unresolved` | The query needs an explicit event/occurrence identity that resemblance alone cannot establish. |
| `correction_scope_unclear` | A field-scoped correction needs the requested field stated explicitly. |

The existing `conflicting_or_multiple_owners`, `retrieval_ambiguous`, source-change,
eligibility, budget and reader diagnostics remain in use. Unique-value ambiguity
requires clarification. Source changes discard old claims, passages and explored
edges. CLI `ask` accepts `--record-id`, `--field` and `--as-of`.

Source pages can declare sealed `event_id` / `occurrence_id` metadata through
`ledger.write`, or explicit `Event-ID:` / `Occurrence-ID:` source body headers.
`inspect_events` retains every appearance as its own `source-id@hash` occurrence,
along with any declared occurrence ID. An event has a distinct `event:` node ID
and its own false support/truth flags. Declared event IDs and generated shared-key
nodes occupy separate identity namespaces, even when their display labels match. A source declaration is not a historical
identity certification.

A new shared-key event candidate requires at least two appearances declaring the
same explicit `Event-Key:`. A repeated message ID, equal subject or equal date
alone does not create an event. Changed bodies under a common message key remain
visible for review. Original appearances are never merged or overwritten.

```python
from mplpb_combined.ledger import write
correction = write(root, doc_id='SRC-2', title='Correction', scope='archive owner',
    supersedes=['SRC-1@sha256:...'], corrects_field='Owner',
    valid_from='2026-01-01', valid_until='2027-01-01',
    body='Record-ID: CASE-1\nOwner: Bob')
result = answer_query(root, 'What is Owner for record CASE-1?', as_of='2025-12-31')
```

`corrects-field`, `valid-from` and `valid-until` are sealed optional fields. Old
pages retain their hashes because absent optional fields do not enter their
hashes. `supersedes` pins must resolve exactly. Dates mean midnight UTC;
timestamps require an explicit timezone. The lower bound is inclusive and the
upper bound exclusive. Invalid or reversed windows are rejected. The default
view uses current UTC time. Queries outside a declared correction window see the
pinned predecessor, subject to all its original eligibility checks. Queries for
other fields also use the predecessor. Field-scoped correction sources require an explicit matching field selector at
the provenance gate; generic source reads cannot bypass this restriction. No page
bytes or status lines are rewritten by a read. Query contexts are isolated and reset after success or failure.

Withdrawing a correction never restores its predecessor, including in an as-of
query. A valid standalone withdrawal in its successor chain remains an eligibility
barrier. Restoration still requires a new explicit revision. Query views do not
authorize edits to old nonterminal heads. This is declared-window serving, not
arbitrary reconstruction of the entire ledger at a historical time.

`correct_claim` and CLI `correct-claim` also accept `corrects_field`, `valid_from`
and `valid_until` (`--corrects-field`, `--valid-from`, `--valid-until`). A field
correction must name the complete unique field line and preserve its label. The
predecessor and unaffected text remain inspectable. Unrelated claim text is not
automatically corrected or inferred.

`answer_query(..., relation_hops=[...])` accepts one or two explicit hop objects:
`question`, `source_id`, `hash`, `quote`. Each question must fit a current
relation-graph family. Each edge independently reloads eligible source evidence
and verifies its full source quote and pin. Consecutive subject/value keys must
match. A missing quote, restricted/changed source, unsupported question or missing
link produces a candidate edge. Causal chains and reverse causal inference are
not licensed. Three or more hops are rejected.

The `exploration` result records each edge, family, direction, quotation and
verification status. Even fully quoted edges remain an inspection graph;
exploration never composes a supported answer. Existing deterministic direct
answering remains available by omitting this optional mode.

Completion receipts retain false answer/truth flags. Host-only
`WorkStore.record_external_receipt` records separate STORE, DISPATCH, DELIVERY,
READ, ACK and COMPLETION observations tied to an execution receipt. Linked stages
require the correct preceding observation; legacy standalone READ/ACK cannot
bridge a checked chain. Optional bounded local STORE byte checks and host-only
`verify_storage_receipt` rechecks are described in the [solo workflow](SOLO_RESEARCH_WORKFLOW.md). These are host declarations,
not independent external-world verification. They cannot become claim evidence,
change a source pin, or promote a claim. Existing dispatch fencing, reconciliation
and recheck-on-source-change rules remain in force. Work source checks always use
the present serving view: a historical query context cannot authorize work from
a source that is retired today. The seat RPC does not expose
this host operation. Handoffs always retain `answer_supported:false` and
`content_truth_verified:false`.

`WorkStore.put(..., operator_seconds=2.5)` attaches optional self-reported effort
to that work event. Trusted host adapters may return `operator_seconds` and
`operator_seconds_basis` (`measured` or `self_reported`). No execution duration is
automatically labelled human effort. Values must be finite nonnegative numbers;
booleans are rejected. Effort never affects eligibility, assessment or answer
support. Handoffs expose only visible, readable event measurements and their sum;
unknown effort is `null`, not zero. Private effort does not leak through another
seat's view.

Study reviewers can optionally supply `operator_seconds` per case. Scoring reports
their total separately from `work_event_operator_seconds` captured by the engine.
Missing measurements stay `null`; reviewer measurements and identities remain
unattested. This adds instrumentation, not a completed operator-burden study or
independent human validation.
